titles.title: Quake1
titles.engine: id Quake: GLQUAKE.EXE (id gl_vidnt.c build, md5 bcf4049319feb518b8c915ac1cc8219b, 'Exe: 15:17:32 Nov 7 1997'; the title plate reads '(GL 0.97) 1.09'; VOODOO\GLQUAKE.EXE is byte-identical) on 1.08 data. WINQUAKE.EXE (software, md5 0b62b82dea48408f45369e1fab53eb0c) is a second shortcut.
titles.launch_sets: 800x600x32 fullscreen on all four 1080p LCDs, caused by the launcher's own -cap. RE-MEASURED 2026-09-29 00:3x: I ran each box's DEPLOYED C:\Games\Quake1\FLEETRES.EXE -cmd -cap 1280 960. On .123, .145, .195 and .240 alike it returned FR_W/H=1280x720 and FR_W43/H43=800x600, and FR_LIVE/FR_DESK=1920x1080. Play Quake.bat passes GLQUAKE.EXE -width %FR_W43% -height %FR_H43% -bpp 32. fleetres.c 787-799 keeps the panel's 16:9 aspect under the cap (1280x720), and the classic 4:3 ladder under a 720-line target stops at 800x600. PER-TITLE-STATUS ('capped 1280x960') is wrong. The .246 compat note that blames GLQuake's table is also wrong. The compat DB measured 800x600 on .123, .240 and .246/.195. The deployed launcher equals the staged one on all four boxes (md5 b263c4414c). There is no GAMERES rule (command-line title). The Software shortcut passes no mode.
titles.menu_source: Options > Video Modes is READ-ONLY. It prints 'Video modes must be set from the command line with -width...' and has no selectable control. The list is driver-enumerated, not a fixed table. VID_InitFullDIB takes EnumDisplaySettings modes with bpp>=15 that pass CDS_TEST, one slot per WxHxBPP, and stops at 30 slots (cmp 0x1e at 0x415881). Slot 0 is the windowed mode, which leaves 29. MEASURED ON .123 (ATI HD 3850, XP): I ran a windowed GLQuake with vid_describemodes in the console and took a screenshot. The ATI driver enumerates RESOLUTION-MAJOR, 16 then 32 bpp per resolution, and the list ends at '29: 1920x1080x16 fullscreen'. 1920x1080x32 does not fit, so the launcher's -bpp 32 can never reach 1080p there, and today's page shows 1920x1080x16 only as text. The order is per driver. .145's measurements (glh2 1920x1080 works at 16 bpp, GLQuake -bpp 32 fails) fit bpp-major. .240's list starts with six sub-640 modes, so if it is resolution-major like .123 it fills at 1280x720x16 (inferred from the 2026-08-31 glh2 failures). With -current, every entry reads 'Desktop resolution (1920x1080)' (measured, screenshot 02); it is still not selectable. WINQUAKE.EXE's menu is selectable, but only for 8-bpp modes with w<=1280 and h<=1024 (cmp 0x500/0x400 at 0x40c83d).

titles.fix: Launcher change using stock switches, VERIFIED on .123 hardware (the switches were typed by hand, not run through a launcher): GLQUAKE.EXE -current -conwidth %FR_CONW% -conheight %FR_CONH% +fov %FR_FOV%, where FR_CONW=FR_W/2 and FR_CONH=FR_H/2 are computed per box. That gives 960x540 on the 1080p LCDs and 512x384 on a 1024x768 CRT. FR_W/H must come from an UNCAPPED FLEETRES call. Use -current only when FR_LIVE_W x FR_LIVE_H equals that FR_W x FR_H. Otherwise keep TODAY's capped call (-cap 1280 960, i.e. 800x600, which is proven), so call FLEETRES twice or save the capped values separately. The .123 run was `-current -conwidth 960 -conheight 540 +fov 106`. It gave a borderless GLQuake window at 0,0-1920x1080, the desktop mode never changed, engine F11 frames came out 1920x1080 with proportionate geometry and a 2x HUD, and the Video Modes page showed 'Desktop resolution (1920x1080)'. Three corrections to the prior proposal. (1) Hardcoding -conwidth 960 -conheight 540 is wrong. -current also fires on the 4:3 CRT boxes, and R_SetupGL projects from vid (= con) coordinates, so a 16:9 console there squashes the picture horizontally. (2) The fallback must not be an uncapped -width %FR_W43% -height %FR_H43% -bpp 32. 1280x960x32 is slot 20 on .123, but on .240 (and possibly .195) it falls outside the 29 slots, and a miss is a hard Sys_Error. (3) There is no selectable in-game resolution control with stock GLQuake or WinQuake. Only a port such as QuakeSpasm gives one. None is on the share: a case-insensitive find over Files, Utility, DiskImages and transmission found none.
titles.fix_source: Already in the staged GLQUAKE.EXE: '-current' @0x450e20 (code 0x415e3d sets modelist[1] from GetSystemMetrics, vid_default=1 and leavecurrentmode [0x8094a0]=1; VID_SetFullDIBMode @0x414470 then skips ChangeDisplaySettingsA), '-conwidth'/'-conheight' @0x450de0/0x450dd4, and 'Desktop resolution (%dx%d)'. The launcher text is generated by scripts/fleet/stage-fleetres.py (NEW_GLQUAKE, and the GLQUAKE.EXE branch of new_launcher that emits call_cap(1280, 960)). FR_CONW/FR_CONH can be computed with set /a in the launcher, or added to fleetres.c followed by a FLEETRES.EXE rebuild and re-stage. A selectable in-game menu would need a port download (QuakeSpasm, sourceforge); none is on the share.
titles.fix_risk: Low. -current is a borderless window at the live desktop mode, not an exclusive mode set. The window covered the screen on .123 and the taskbar was hidden. No mode change happens at start, so nothing needs restoring on exit. On alt-tab back, AppActivate calls ChangeDisplaySettings with an empty gdevmode, which should be harmless (not tested). Unmeasured: Win7 .195 (DWM), .145, .240, and the Voodoo 5 box .124, where 'Play Quake - Voodoo.bat' calls 'Play Quake.bat' on a VSA-100 and so reaches -current through the Glide-backed ICD. The protocol is unchanged, so the NetQuake server at 192.168.1.132:26000 is unaffected (join not re-tested). Tests to change in the same commit: tests/python/test_fleetres_staging.py test_only_the_measured_ceilings_carry_a_cap and test_glquake_cap_is_the_measured_ceiling_not_the_old_guess. PROCESS RISK THAT BIT THIS REVIEW: every LCD box was in use by other agents' game tests, and two of my launches on .123 minimized other agents' sessions (details in verifier_notes).
titles.hw_check: Only on an idle box: check WINLIST and PROCLIST immediately before launching, and never chain the check and the launch in one command. (1) Today: EXEC cmd /c start "" /D "C:\Games\Quake1" "Play Quake.bat"; DISPLAYCFG get should read 800x600x32. (2) Mode list: GLQUAKE.EXE -window -width 1280 -height 960 -conwidth 1280 -conheight 960 +toggleconsole +vid_describemodes, then SCREENSHOT 0 (done on .123). DO NOT use the prior proposal's -condebug + qconsole.log route. Con_DebugLog vsprintf's into a 1 KB static buffer that sits directly before the console-text pointer, and GL_EXTENSIONS is 3.8 KB on .123. The -condebug run there exited within 9 s, right after logging that line. (3) Fix proof: -current -conwidth <FR_W/2> -conheight <FR_H/2> +fov <FR_FOV>. WINLIST must show GLQuake at 0,0-1920x1080 and DISPLAYCFG must stay 1920x1080x32. Press F11: id1\quakeNN.tga must be 6,220,818 B (1920x1080). Then keys (they work fullscreen): ESCAPE, DOWN, DOWN, RETURN, UP, RETURN; the Video Modes page must read 'Desktop resolution (1920x1080)'. Then connect 192.168.1.132. Repeat on .145, .240 and .195; on .195, use the F11 TGA if GDI comes back black. Clean up: taskkill /f /im "GLQUAKE.EXE" and DELETE the new TGAs (quake00/01.tga on .123 predate this review).
titles.verifier_notes: CONFIRMED on hardware: the launch_sets numbers (800x600 on all four, from the deployed FLEETRES.EXE), the read-only menu, the 30-slot cap (measured list on .123 ends at slot 29 = 1920x1080x16), and -current (verified working at 1920x1080 on .123). CHANGED: (a) the fix: per-box -conwidth/-conheight instead of 960x540; fallback = keep the proven cap, not an uncapped -bpp 32 request. (b) fix_risk: the prior text said the read-only menu 'keeps the old label on mode 1'. It actually shows 'Desktop resolution (1920x1080)' for every entry (measured). (c) hw_check: removed -condebug, which crashes GLQuake (measured exit plus disassembly). (d) menu_source: the enumeration order is per driver (ATI .123 resolution-major, measured), so which 1080p depth fits varies by box. DISCLOSURE: at about 00:33:30 and about 00:54:30 EDT my windowed GLQuake launches on .123 took focus from other agents' Carmageddon II (pid 1468) and Descent 3 (pid 1864) fullscreen sessions. Both windows were minimized and the desktop returned to 1920x1080. Evidence those agents captured in those minutes is disturbed, not a game fault. I sent the orchestrator (main) a message about it, then stopped launching on shared boxes.

titles.title: Quake2Complete
titles.engine: id Tech 2: retail Quake II 3.20 (quake2.exe md5 57dd2cf4ba176f3e6ae72fccc94c38b4, 'Oct 16 1998 Win32 RELEASE'; ref_gl.dll b6d33427..., ref_soft.dll 203dc879...), with baseq2, xatrix, rogue and ctf. A second 3.20 copy under Files/Games/Windows XP/Quake2 differs only in the DOS stub (aea5be5f...).
titles.launch_sets: 1280x960 fullscreen (gl_mode 8) on all four LCDs. Each of the 4 launchers calls FLEETRES with no cap, writes <mod>\fleetres.cfg (set gl_mode "%FR_Q2MODE%" plus vid_fullscreen 1), and passes +set gl_mode %FR_Q2MODE%. The autoexec.cfg in baseq2, xatrix, rogue and ctf each ends with exec fleetres.cfg (checked all four). The GAMERES idtech2 rule (gameres.h 702-705, body 867-870) writes the same file. Re-measured today: the deployed FLEETRES.EXE -info reports q2mode 8 on .123, .145, .195 and .240, and GAMERES target.q2mode is 8 on all four. Measured 1280x960 on .123, .240 and .246/.195 (the .246 F11 TGA is 1280x960). The only 1024x768 record, .145 on 2026-09-01, predates today's values. Deployed launchers equal staged. 1280x960 is 4:3, so the panel scaler stretches or pillarboxes it.
titles.menu_source: Hardcoded in quake2.exe. vid_modes[] is at file offset 0x543d0: exactly 10 entries of {desc,w,h,mode}, 'Mode 0: 320x240'..'Mode 9: 1600x1200'; entry [10] is not a mode. The Video menu's 'video mode' spinner uses a separate label-pointer array at file offset 0x54678: '[320 240  ]'..'[1600 1200]' then NULL (10 labels). The menu index IS gl_mode. ref_gl gets its size only via Vid_GetModeInfo(gl_mode). There is no custom mode and no 16:9 entry.
titles.evidence: .claude/evidence-1080p/static-idtech12-doom3/menus/idtech2_vid_modes_tables.txt and quake2_320_modes_and_menu.txt (offsets re-checked with pefile: table at 0x543d0, 10 entries; label array at 0x54678); .claude/evidence-1080p/review-idtech12-doom3/{123,145,195,240}-fleetres-caps.txt (q2mode 8 on all four); /mnt/retro-share/Files/Games-Library/Quake2Complete/Quake II*.bat and {baseq2,xatrix,rogue,ctf}/autoexec.cfg; agent/shared/gameres.h 295-330, 470, 702-705, 867-870; compat records in .claude/evidence-1080p/static-idtech12-doom3/compat_render_measured.txt.
titles.fix: There is no config-only route in 3.20. Byte-patch Quake2Complete's quake2.exe only: vid_modes[9] width @0x54464 1600->1920 and height @0x54468 1200->1080, plus the same-length strings 'Mode 9: 1600x1200'->'Mode 9: 1920x1080' and label '[1600 1200]'->'[1920 1080]' (file offset 0x54720). No fleet box uses gl_mode 9 today; the CRT boxes resolve to 4, 6 or 8. ADDITION the prior answer glossed over: FR_Q2MODE feeds three titles (Quake2Complete x4, SiNGold x3 including the software sw_mode launcher, SoF x1). Choosing 9 for a 1920x1080 target therefore needs a NEW, separately named value (for example FR_Q2WIDE), not a change to FR_Q2MODE. The same value must be added identically in fleetres.c and gameres.h, and both the launchers and the GAMERES idtech2 body must use it. The two writers of <mod>\fleetres.cfg would otherwise rewrite each other on every sync (tests/python/test_gameres_mirror.py, test_a_shared_cfg_is_written_identically_by_both_writers). Add set fov %FR_FOV% to both writers as well. Alternative client: Yamagi Quake II (r_mode -1 plus a real video menu). It speaks protocol 34 like the fleet's Yamagi 8.60 server. An XP-buildable fork exists (web-verified: github.com/akosela/yquake2-xp, forked from 8.01); whether it ships release binaries is unverified. No Yamagi, KMQuake2, Q2PRO or R1Q2 build is on the share (case-insensitive search).
titles.fix_source: The patch needs no download: the bytes are in the staged quake2.exe at the offsets above. The selection logic lives in provisioning/fleetres/fleetres.c and agent/shared/gameres.h. FLEETRES.EXE must be rebuilt and re-staged into every title by scripts/fleet/stage-fleetres.py. gameres.h is compiled into the agent, so the agent needs a version bump and publish. Yamagi-XP would have to be downloaded from github.com/akosela/yquake2-xp, together with Yamagi-built game DLLs for baseq2, xatrix, rogue and ctf.
titles.fix_risk: The patch modifies a retail exe shared by 4 launchers. 3.20 draws the HUD, console and menus at 1:1 pixels, so they are tiny at 1080p. Never point ref_soft at mode 9 (the id GPL ref_soft MAXWIDTH is 1600; source knowledge, not binary-verified). Quake2Win9x ships the identical exe; leave that copy stock. ROLLOUT RISK: until every box runs an agent with the new gameres.h, an old agent writes gl_mode 8 and a new launcher writes 9 into the same fleetres.cfg on each sync. The launcher writes last and also passes +set, so the game still starts at 9, but GAMERES never settles to '0 value(s) changed' during the rollout. Multiplayer: protocol 34 has no exe or pure check, so a join to 192.168.1.132:27910 should be unaffected; prove it with one join.
titles.hw_check: EXEC cmd /c start "" /D "C:\Games\Quake2Complete" "Quake II.bat" on an idle box; DISPLAYCFG get should read 1280x960. The menu is keyboard-navigable: Esc > Options > Video, then the arrow keys cycle 'video mode'. Press F11 for baseq2\scrnshot\quakeNN.tga, or use GDI SCREENSHOT 0 on the XP boxes. The list should end at [1600 1200]. After the patch: the last entry should read [1920 1080], applying it should give DISPLAYCFG 1920x1080 and a 1920x1080 frame, `connect 192.168.1.132:27910` should still join, and two consecutive GAMESYNC/GAMERES APPLY runs should report 0 value(s) changed.
titles.verifier_notes: Confirmed (table and label offsets re-checked; q2mode 8 re-measured on all four boxes; every mod's autoexec ends with exec fleetres.cfg). Added: FR_Q2MODE feeds three titles, so a separate value is needed and it must change identically in fleetres.c and gameres.h (both write fleetres.cfg), with the agent-rollout churn noted; the Yamagi XP fork is web-verified. The prior note is correct that the staged autoexec comment's 'autoexec runs BEFORE VID_Init' is wrong: in id's CL_Init, FS_ExecAutoexec runs after VID_Init.

titles.title: HexenII
titles.engine: Raven Hexen II retail 1.03. glh2.exe is a GLQuake-derived OpenGL build (md5 c450ea8ac9aefa9e4a5b48e9c7ae4e66, 'Exe: 15:08:09 Sep 4 1997'; VOODOO\GLH2.EXE is identical). h2.exe is the software build (md5 7ad8abed...).
titles.launch_sets: Not 1080p, and it differs by box. RE-MEASURED 2026-09-29: the deployed C:\Games\HexenII\FLEETRES.EXE -cmd -cap 1024 768 returns FR_W/H=848x480 on .123 and .240, and 1024x768 on .145 and .195. The Play, Host and Join launchers pass glh2.exe -width %FR_W% -height %FR_H% with no -bpp, so glh2 tries 15 bpp, then 16. The compat DB measured 848x480 on .123/.240 and 1024x768x16 on .246/.195 (DISPLAYCFG). The deployed launchers equal the staged ones. There is no GAMERES rule. The 2026-08-31 -cap was added to the share outside the generator: stage-fleetres.py TITLES['HexenII'] has no cap, and test_hexen2_is_not_capped_like_glquake pins that. `stage-fleetres.py --check` still reports all 213 launchers as current (run today; its 1 failure is Thief2), so it cannot see this drift. PER-TITLE-STATUS's '1080p, measured on .145' predates the cap.
titles.menu_source: Options > Video Modes is the same READ-ONLY GLQuake page (the 'Fullscreen Modes (WIDTHxHEIGHTxBPP)' and 'Video modes must be set from the...' strings are in glh2.exe). Its entries are the driver-enumerated modelist with the same 30-slot cap (cmp ecx,0x1e at 0x4308e2). That explains both measurements: .240 refused 1280x960, 1280x1024 and 1920x1080, while .145 accepted 1920x1080 at 16 bpp. The same enumeration, measured for GLQuake on .123, is resolution-major and ends at 1920x1080x16. What appears differs by box, and nothing on the page can be selected. With -current the entries become 'Desktop resolution (%dx%d)' (the string is in glh2). h2.exe's menu is selectable but takes 8-bpp modes only, w<=1280, h<=1024 (0x415e6d).
titles.evidence: /mnt/retro-share/Files/Games-Library/HexenII/{Play Hexen II.bat, Host Hexen II - LAN.bat, Join Hexen II - LAN.bat} (-cap 1024 768); .claude/evidence-1080p/review-idtech12-doom3/{123,145,195,240}-fleetres-caps.txt; .claude/evidence-1080p/review-idtech12-doom3/static/glh2-current-and-projection.txt (-current at 0x430e32 sets vid_default [0x4680a8] and leavecurrentmode [0x7cb948]; VID_SetFullDIBMode 0x42f550 skips ChangeDisplaySettings when it is set; vid 320x200 fixed at 0x42f708; R_SetupGL 0x407bb0 projection); .claude/evidence-1080p/static-idtech12-doom3/disasm/hexen2_modelist_cap30.txt; scripts/fleet/stage-fleetres.py 1038-1060; tests/python/test_lan_multiplayer_library.py 44-99 and test_fleetres_staging.py 739-746.
titles.fix: Launch change: glh2.exe -current -heapsize 32768 -nocdaudio (plus the Host/Join extras). This is statically confirmed: the -current path sets leavecurrentmode [0x7cb948] and VID_SetFullDIBMode skips ChangeDisplaySettings, the same code as GLQuake, whose -current I verified on .123. Guard it with FR_LIVE == FR_W/H from an UNCAPPED FLEETRES call. CORRECTION: the fallback must keep today's -cap 1024 768 path, which is measured working. It must not be an uncapped -width %FR_W43% -height %FR_H43% (1280x960), because that was measured failing on .240 with 'Specified video mode not available'. The failure happens before the listen server opens, so the Host LAN launcher would silently host nothing. -current can never hit that check. NEW FINDING on aspect (static): glh2 has no -conwidth switch at all. Its vid is fixed at 320x200 (0x42f708). R_SetupGL scales vrect by glwidth/320 and glheight/200 and calls MYgluPerspective(fovy=2*atan(h/w), aspect=w/h) on that 320x200-space vrect (constant 114.59=360/pi at 0x45a130). So horizontal FOV is always 90, the fov cvar is ignored, and the picture is correct only on 16:10. It is about 11% horizontally stretched at 16:9 (1920x1080 via -current, and today's 848x480) and about 17% horizontally squashed at 4:3 (today's 1024x768 on .145/.195). -current improves resolution and error size but cannot fix the aspect. Only a port (uHexen2 / Hammer of Thyrion) gives a correct aspect and an in-game resolution menu; none is on the share (case-insensitive search for hexen2, uhexen2, thyrion, glhexen).
titles.fix_source: -current is already in the staged glh2.exe (string @0x468a48). The launcher recipe lives in scripts/fleet/stage-fleetres.py TITLES['HexenII']; its 'fix' list must also cover the -cap text, which was added outside the generator. A port would need downloading (uHexen2 1.5.x, sourceforge.net/projects/uhexen2).
titles.fix_risk: Low to medium. It is a stock switch but depends on the live desktop mode (hence the guard). The 11% 16:9 stretch is inherent to this 1997 build (static finding, unmeasured). LAN: the tests test_hexen2_gl_launchers_cap_to_a_mode_the_engine_has and _cap_the_engine_at_1024x768 require the cap and must be rewritten alongside. The latter's docstring claims -cap 1024 768 yields FR_W=1024 FR_H=768 on hardware, which is false on .123/.240 (848x480, re-measured today). Its assertion only checks the cap numbers. Host and join must be re-proven on two boxes with scripts/game-servers/nqquery.py <ip> 26900 HEXENII. .124's Voodoo launcher calls 'Play Hexen II.bat' on a VSA-100 and would inherit -current (unmeasured).
titles.hw_check: On an idle box: EXEC cmd /c start "" /D "C:\Games\HexenII" "Play Hexen II.bat"; DISPLAYCFG get should read 848x480 on .123/.240 and 1024x768x16 on .145/.195. The menu is keyboard-navigable: Esc > Options > Video Modes. The GL build's F11 writes data1\shots\hexenNN.TGA ('shots/hexen00.tga' in glh2), not .pcx as the README says; on XP, GDI SCREENSHOT 0 also works. Fix proof: glh2.exe -current -heapsize 32768 -nocdaudio. WINLIST should show class HexenII at 0,0-1920x1080, DISPLAYCFG should stay 1920x1080x32, the frame should be 1920x1080, and a round object should look about 11% wide. Then Host with -current on one box, confirm nqquery.py <ip> 26900 HEXENII answers, join from a second box, and screenshot both. Delete the new TGAs and taskkill /f /im "glh2.exe".
titles.verifier_notes: Launch_sets confirmed on hardware (848x480 on .123/.240, 1024x768 on .145/.195 from the deployed FLEETRES.EXE). -current confirmed by disassembly: the prior evidence file showed only the vid_default store, and I located the leavecurrentmode store and the check in VID_SetFullDIBMode. CHANGED: (1) the fallback keeps the measured cap instead of an uncapped FR_W43 request; (2) the 'aspect unknown' note is replaced by a static finding that the fixed 320x200 virtual screen means an 11% stretch at 16:9 and a 17% squash at 4:3, with the fov cvar ignored; (3) the screenshot is TGA not PCX; (4) the test's FR_W=1024 claim lives in its docstring, not its assertion. No hardware run of glh2 -current: every LCD box was busy with other agents' tests.

titles.title: SiNGold
titles.engine: Ritual SiN (id Tech 2 derivative) at the official 1.11 (sin.exe md5 8d320d7fc3ea3a226ec98dafef3e81ba, 'Jan 22 2001'), with Wages of SiN (2015\) and ctf\. The GOG 1.13b rebuild that was replaced is kept in _patches (see fix_source).
titles.launch_sets: 1280x960 fullscreen (gl_mode 8) through Play SiN Gold.bat and Play Wages of SiN.bat. Each calls FLEETRES, writes base\ or 2015\fleetres.cfg (gl_mode %FR_Q2MODE% plus vid_fullscreen), and passes +set gl_mode. Both autoexec.cfg files set gl_mode 6 and end with exec fleetres.cfg, so 8 wins. GAMERES idtech2 rows cover base and 2015. FR_Q2MODE is 8 on all four boxes (re-measured). Measured 1280x960 on .123/.240 (verified) and .246/.195 (runs). Deployed launchers equal staged. .145 crashes in every OpenGL context (README-CDCHECK: the log ends at GL_VERSION 3.3.0, before GL_EXTENSIONS), so only 'Play SiN - software renderer.bat' works there. CORRECTION: that launcher's +set sw_mode %FR_Q2MODE% (8) does not survive. It is an EARLY +set, base\autoexec.cfg runs later and sets sw_mode "6" (line 107), and the software launcher writes no fleetres.cfg (fleetres.cfg sets only gl_mode anyway). The software path therefore settles at mode 6 = 1024x768, which matches the verified .145 run (static inference from the Quake II startup order, not re-measured).
titles.menu_source: Menu data file menus/main.mnu, used at 640x480 and above (sin.exe 0x429c3a: width>=0x280 and height>=0x1e0 selects main.mnu, else main_alt.mnu). Path: main menu > Controls > Video > 'Video Mode:', listitem con_vidmode. base\pak5.sin (1.11) has numitems 10, ' 320 x 240'..' 1600 x 1200'. 2015\pak0.sin has numitems 9, so Wages stops at 1280 x 960. ctf\pak1.sin carries its own 10-item copy. apply_vid_changes copies con_vidmode into gl_mode and sw_mode, which index sin.exe's vid_modes (file offset 0x94450, Mode 0 320x240 .. Mode 9 1600x1200, 10 entries).
titles.evidence: .claude/evidence-1080p/static-idtech12-doom3/menus/sin_main_mnu_video_mode.txt and idtech2_vid_modes_tables.txt (table re-checked); .claude/evidence-1080p/review-idtech12-doom3/static/sin-menu-sync.txt (menu_main 0x44a8e0 -> vid_reset 0x44a050: con_vidmode=gl_mode when vid_ref is 'gl'; main vs main_alt at 0x429c3a; FS_AddGameDirectory 0x441ef0: pak0-31 then the loose directory PREPENDED, so loose files win); .claude/evidence-1080p/review-idtech12-doom3/static/sin-gog-1.13b-widescreen-table.txt; /mnt/retro-share/Files/Games-Library/SiNGold/{Play SiN Gold.bat, Play Wages of SiN.bat, Play SiN - software renderer.bat, base/autoexec.cfg 61-64,106-108,177, 2015/autoexec.cfg 73-76,118-120,189, README-RESTAGE.txt, README-CDCHECK.txt}; gameres.h 706-707.
titles.fix: Same shape as Quake II. Patch 1.11 sin.exe vid_modes[9]: width @0x944e4 1600->1920, height @0x944e8 1200->1080, string 'Mode 9: 1600x1200'->'Mode 9: 1920x1080'. Relabel the menu, but NO PAK IS NEEDED, which corrects the prior 'pak required (inferred)'. SiN's FS_AddGameDirectory loads pak0-31 and then prepends the loose directory, so loose files override that directory's paks. Ship loose base\menus\main.mnu (copy of pak5's, ' 1600 x 1200'->' 1920 x 1080') and 2015\menus\main.mnu (copy of 2015\pak0's, same relabel plus numitems 9->10). main_alt.mnu only matters below 640x480. Then implement the separate 1080p gl_mode value identically in FLEETRES and GAMERES (see Quake2Complete). Keep the software launcher off mode 9; today its sw_mode is overridden to 6 anyway. REFUTED: the prior claim that 'No SiN widescreen fix is on the share'. The GOG SiN Gold 1.13b rebuild on the share already has a widescreen table: 'Mode 0: 640x480' .. 'Mode 11: 1280x720 (Widescreen)', 'Mode 12: 1920x1080 (Widescreen)' .. 'Mode 14: 3840x2160'. It is NOT usable as-is. It is an MSVC-2015 build with subsystem/OS 6.0, which XP's loader refuses. It imports VCRUNTIME140 and api-ms-win-crt-*, needs SSE2 libm, and its mode numbers differ from 1.11's. README-RESTAGE records that on Win7 .246 it 'exits immediately with RC=0' (cause never found). At most it is a lead for .195 only. UNTESTED LEAD for .145's GL crash (without it the 1080p patch never reaches that box): NVIDIA's per-application OpenGL 'Extension limit' control-panel setting targets exactly this class of old id-lineage crash on long extension strings. Its availability on .145's driver is unverified.
titles.fix_source: No download: the bytes are in the staged sin.exe, the menus are in base\pak5.sin and 2015\pak0.sin (extract, edit, ship loose). The GOG build is at /mnt/retro-share/Files/Games-Library/_patches/backup-2026-08-29/SiNGold/gog-1.13b-binaries/sin.exe (md5 131399874914033b73d439733663dc47) and in Files/Games/Windows XP/setup_sin_gold_1.13b_(36951).exe.
titles.fix_risk: Medium. It modifies the 1.11 exe, the same file that solved the CD check; keep the original. SiN's menus and HUD are laid out for 4:3 and are unmeasured at 16:9. Never send ref_soft_real.dll to mode 9. The same FLEETRES/GAMERES lockstep and rollout risk as Quake II applies. Multiplayer is box-to-box via ds_*.bat with no pure check; prove one join. The video-menu presets (vm_hw_low/mid/high.cfg) set gl_mode 2 or 3 and vid_restart, so clicking one drops to 512x384 or 640x480 until the next launch.
titles.hw_check: On an idle box other than .145: EXEC cmd /c start "" /D "C:\Games\SiNGold" "Play SiN Gold.bat"; DISPLAYCFG get should read 1280x960. Menu path: main menu > Controls > Video > 'Video Mode:'. It should show ' 1280 x 960' (menu_main runs vid_reset, which copies gl_mode into con_vidmode) and end at ' 1600 x 1200', or at ' 1280 x 960' in Wages of SiN. Keyboard navigation of this menu is still unproven on the fleet. F11 writes base\players\<name>\scrnshot\sin###.tga; on XP, GDI SCREENSHOT 0 also works. On .145, check the software shortcut: DISPLAYCFG should read 1024x768 (not 1280x960).
titles.verifier_notes: CHANGED: (1) The prior verifier note ('menu shows 1024 x 768 while running 1280x960; Apply drops to 1024x768') is refuted by disassembly, not measured. The menu_main command (0x44a8e0) calls vid_reset (0x44a050), which sets con_vidmode from gl_mode under vid_ref gl, so the list shows the running mode and Apply keeps it. (2) 'A pak is required, loose files are shadowed' is wrong for SiN: its file system searches the loose directory first; it is right for SoF. (3) The software-renderer launch_sets was corrected: autoexec's sw_mode 6 wins, giving 1024x768, not 1280x960. (4) 'No SiN widescreen fix on the share' was corrected: the GOG 1.13b build has a 1920x1080 mode but is not viable on XP. (5) Added the .145 extension-limit lead. Table offsets and menu contents confirmed.

titles.title: SoldierOfFortune
titles.engine: Raven Soldier of Fortune (id Tech 2 + GHOUL). It shows 1.03 x86F on screen (SoF.exe md5 2f4db3771d51d8b585bbea695041e40c). The last official patch, 1.07f, is not on the share; Files/Games/Windows XP/Soldier of Fortune (2000).zip is only the CD image (bin/cue).
titles.launch_sets: 1280x960 fullscreen (gl_mode 8). Play Soldier of Fortune.bat calls FLEETRES, writes base\fleetres.cfg (gl_mode %FR_Q2MODE% plus vid_fullscreen), and passes +set gl_mode. base\autoexec.cfg ends with exec fleetres.cfg. The GAMERES idtech2 row covers base. FR_Q2MODE is 8 on all four boxes (re-measured). Measured 1280x960 on .123 (verified, ARC menu) and .240 (runs, window 0,0-1280x960); .246/.195 runs with the resolution unrecorded; .145 has no record. The deployed launcher equals the staged one. No level loads anywhere: every map raises the WON 'insert the SOF CD' error (requires.json, re-measured 2026-09-28 on .124), so only the menus can be verified at any resolution.
titles.menu_source: RMF text menu menus/m_video.rmf, only in base\pak0.pak (pak1.pak holds no menus): <list "640x480,800x600,960x720,1024x768,1152x864,1280x960,1600x1200" match "3,4,5,6,7,8,9" cvar menu_mode>. Opening the video menu runs menus/video.cfg (set menu_mode $gl_mode), so the list shows the running mode. 'Apply' runs menus/applyvid.cfg (set gl_mode $menu_mode; vid_restart). SoF.exe's vid_modes table at file offset 0x1c6e08 holds 'Mode 0/1/2: Unsupported' (320x240, 400x300, 512x384), then 'Mode 3: 640x480'..'Mode 9: 1600x1200'.
titles.evidence: .claude/evidence-1080p/static-idtech12-doom3/menus/sof_m_video_rmf.txt and idtech2_vid_modes_tables.txt (re-checked); .claude/evidence-1080p/review-idtech12-doom3/static/sof-fs-order-and-menu-sync.txt (FS_AddGameDirectory: loose directory first, then pak0-9 prepended, so paks win; menus/video.cfg); /mnt/retro-share/Files/Games-Library/SoldierOfFortune/{Play Soldier of Fortune.bat, base/autoexec.cfg, README-FLEET.txt, requires.json}; web: sof1.megalag.org/widescreen/ and sof1.megalag.org/sofplus/.
titles.fix: (a) In-tree: patch SoF.exe vid_modes[9] (width @0x1c6e9c 1600->1920, height @0x1c6ea0 1200->1080). Ship base\pak2.pak with an edited menus/m_video.rmf (relabel '1600x1200' as '1920x1080', mapped to 9). A pak IS required here: SoF adds the loose directory first and then prepends pak0-9, so a loose m_video.rmf would be shadowed by pak0.pak. pak2 is within the 0-9 loop. Then use the separate 1080p mode value in FLEETRES and GAMERES in lockstep (see Quake2Complete). (b) The community route, web-verified: SoF 1.07f plus the SoFplus client, whose _sp_cl_vid_mode_0.._9 cvars redefine the modes and whose video menu is overhauled. SoFplus requires 1.07f, and neither is on the share. megalag's own SoF.exe widescreen patch, which does option (a), warns that the bottom of stock menus gets cut off, horizontal FOV stays fixed (vert-), and anti-cheat may complain. It recommends SoFplus instead. Either way, gameplay at 1080p cannot be shown until the WON CD check is solved.
titles.fix_source: (a) No download: the bytes are in the staged SoF.exe, and the menu is in base\pak0.pak. (b) Would need the SoF 1.07f patch and the SoFplus client from sof1.megalag.org. A case-insensitive share search found only the CD image, SoF_Demo.exe and SoF2 material.
titles.fix_risk: Menus clipped at 16:9 (web-reported); FOV fixed (vert-); the exe patch may upset obsolete anti-cheat. There is no multiplayer regression, since multiplayer is already blocked (WON error, no SoF server on the host). Moving to 1.07f changes the version every box presents, so patch the library and move all boxes together.
titles.hw_check: On an idle box: EXEC cmd /c start "" /D "C:\Games\SoldierOfFortune" "Play Soldier of Fortune.bat"; DISPLAYCFG get should read 1280x960. Menu: ARC globe > options folder > Video > 'Resolution', which should read 1280x960. Input evidence conflicts: absolute UICLICK worked on .123, but on .240 the cursor moved by deltas and UIKEY reached nothing. Treat it as needing a human unless a first UICLICK moves the cursor to the clicked point. F11 writes user\scrnshot\sof00.tga (SoF.exe writes under './user'; the staged tree ships user\scrnshot\, and the autoexec comment's base\scrnshot is stale). On XP, GDI SCREENSHOT 0 also works.
titles.verifier_notes: Confirmed (tables, RMF, launch values re-measured, compat records). Added: the pak requirement is correct for SoF, established by the file-system search order in the disassembly. The menu syncs menu_mode from gl_mode on open, so there is no stale-label problem. The screenshot path is user\scrnshot. The prior agent's web claims (SoFplus cvars, 1.07f requirement, menu cut-off, anti-cheat warning) were re-verified on sof1.megalag.org.

titles.title: Doom3
titles.engine: id Tech 4: official DOOM 3 1.3 (version.inf ExtVersion=1.3; DOOM3.exe md5 7cd77c22b38c223ef1047083e374875a, 5,832,704 B, no SafeDisc). base/gamex86.dll (md5 e06f4eb6...) is byte-identical to game03.pk4's 2005-05-10 build. CORRECTION: Resurrection of Evil is NOT installed. d3xp/ holds only the 1.3 patch's overlay: game01-03.pk4 (game DLLs) and pak001.pk4 (99,336 B: mainmenu.gui, mpmain.gui, efx files, one mtr). The RoE content pak (d3xp/pak000.pk4, several hundred MB) is absent from the library and from .123 and .145 (DIRLIST).
titles.launch_sets: 1920x1080 on all four LCDs. Play DOOM 3.bat and Host DOOM 3 - LAN.bat call FLEETRES with no cap and run DOOM3.exe +set r_mode -1 +set r_customWidth %FR_W% +set r_customHeight %FR_H% +set r_aspectRatio %FR_D3AR% +set r_fullscreen 1 (FR_D3AR=1 on 16:9). FR_W/H=1920x1080 on all four (re-measured with the deployed FLEETRES.EXE -info). id Tech 4 re-applies +set after DoomConfig.cfg. r_aspectRatio is defined only in the game DLL (0 hits in DOOM3.exe, 1 in gamex86.dll), and the command-line value survives the DLL's later registration. Measured: 1920x1080 verified on .123 and .240 (2026-08-31), DISPLAYCFG 1920x1080x32 on .246/.195. .145: DOOM 3 has NEVER been started there (C:\Games\Doom3\base has no DoomConfig.cfg and no config.spec). Unexplained observation: .123's DoomConfig.cfg (written 2026-09-01 04:49:59) archives r_mode "3" with r_customWidth/Height 1920/1080 and no r_aspectRatio line. So the last session there ended at r_mode 3, from either a menu touch or R_InitOpenGL's safe-mode fallback. The next launch still passes r_mode -1. Launchers equal staged. Doom3 is still deployed on .240 although today's gate refuses it there for disk (1490 < 1600 MB).
titles.menu_source: base/pak007.pk4 guis/mainmenu.gui (the effective copy, lines 4888-4891) System > 'Screen Size' (#str_02153): choiceDef OS2Primary { choices "#str_04222" values "3;4;5;6;7;8" cvar "r_mode" choiceType 1 }. strings/english.lang: #str_04222 = "640x480;800x600;1024x768;1152x864;1280x1024;1600x1200". DOOM3.exe r_vidModes run from Mode 0 320x240 to Mode 8 1600x1200. There is no aspect control ('aspect' does not occur in the GUI). With r_mode -1, idChoiceWindow falls back to index 0 and shows '640x480' (per id's GPL choice-window logic; not measured). d3xp/pak001.pk4 carries the same choiceDef but is inert without RoE.
titles.evidence: .claude/evidence-1080p/static-idtech12-doom3/menus/doom3_mainmenu_screensize.txt (re-extracted from base/pak007.pk4, identical); .claude/evidence-1080p/review-idtech12-doom3/static/doom3-d3xp-and-config.txt; .claude/evidence-1080p/review-idtech12-doom3/123-Doom3-DoomConfig.cfg (DOWNLOADed from .123); .claude/evidence-1080p/review-idtech12-doom3/{123,145,195,240}-fleetres-caps.txt; /mnt/retro-share/Files/Games-Library/Doom3/{Play DOOM 3.bat, Host DOOM 3 - LAN.bat, version.inf, d3xp/}; scripts/game-servers/doom3/entry.sh (si_pure 0).
titles.fix: Ship base/zz_fleetvideo.pk4, which sorts after pak007.pk4 (Doom 3 prepends pk4s in sorted order, so later names win). It holds a copy of pak007's guis/mainmenu.gui with only the Screen Size choiceDef edited: choices '640x480;800x600;1024x768;1152x864;1280x1024;1600x1200;Native', values '3;4;5;6;7;8;-1'. Use 'Native' rather than '1920x1080', because r_customWidth/Height are per box. Add one choiceDef on r_aspectRatio (choices '4:3;16:9;16:10', values '0;1;2'); that cvar is registered by the game DLL, which is loaded while the menu runs. DROPPED from the prior proposal: d3xp/zz_fleetvideo.pk4. RoE is not installed, so there is nothing to override there until the RoE content pak is staged. No existing fix is on the share: DOOM 3 UPDATE 1.3.exe and classic_doom_3_v1.1.exe are the only related files, dhewm3 is absent and not network-compatible with 1.3, and D3EE is absent.
titles.fix_source: No download: it edits guis/mainmenu.gui from base/pak007.pk4 (696,570 B) and packages it into a new pk4.
titles.fix_risk: Low to medium. It replaces a ~700 KB id GUI script with a copy; diff it against the original so only that choiceDef changes. The fleet doom3-server runs si_pure 0, so an extra client pk4 is fine. On a pure server, client-only paks are excluded and the stock menu returns. The HUD and menus stay 640x480-virtual and stretch at 16:9 (cosmetic). Choosing 'Native' needs r_customWidth/Height already archived; the launcher's +set archives them on the first exit, so .145, which has never run the game, gets them on its first run.
titles.hw_check: On an idle box: EXEC cmd /c start "" /D "C:\Games\Doom3" "Play DOOM 3.bat"; DISPLAYCFG get should read 1920x1080x32. Run it on .145 first, where it has never been run. The menu uses a mouse cursor and is expected to be relative-mouse, so it needs a human unless one UICLICK test proves otherwise. Keyboard-only check: Ctrl+Alt+~, query r_mode, r_customWidth, r_customHeight and r_aspectRatio, run listModes, `condump fleetres_check.txt`, then DOWNLOAD C:\Games\Doom3\base\fleetres_check.txt. On XP boxes, GDI SCREENSHOT 0 captures fullscreen GL, so the Screen Size control can be photographed directly. After the pk4 fix, the Screen Size control must read 'Native' while r_mode is -1. Then DOWNLOAD DoomConfig.cfg after a clean quit and check that r_mode is archived as -1 (it is 3 on .123 today). Delete the dump afterwards.
titles.verifier_notes: CHANGED: (1) 'the d3xp (Resurrection of Evil) paks are present' is wrong. Only the 1.3 patch overlay is present and RoE is not installed, so the d3xp half of the fix and the 'reached through the Mods menu' note are moot. (2) .145 is not just 'untested': DOOM 3 has never been started there (no DoomConfig.cfg or config.spec). (3) Added the .123 observation that the last session archived r_mode 3. Everything else confirmed: the menu choiceDef and string, r_aspectRatio living in the DLL, the launch values (re-measured), si_pure 0, and the gate refusing .240 for disk.
